references.text: This text deals with a man's impurity due to seminal emission and the requirement to wash with water, which directly precedes and parallels the regulation in verse 18 concerning sexual intercourse.
Priests who have experienced seminal emission must not eat of the holy offerings until they have bathed, demonstrating the same period of impurity associated with seminal emission.
Moses commanded the people to keep away from women before the revelation at Sinai, indicating that sexual activity involved a form of ritual impurity.
David assures the priest that his men have kept away from women and that their bodies are clean, reflecting the purity law in Leviticus 15:18.
Impurity lasting until evening and the requirement to wash oneself is a recurring pattern in the purity laws, parallel to the regulation concerning sexual impurity.
Marriage should be held in honor and the marriage bed kept undefiled, which in the New Testament affirms the holiness of marriage and sexual purity.
